lines.speaker: F
lines.text: Audi is putting four billion dollars into its first American factory, and one reason is a fifteen percent tariff on European cars.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: A German carmaker answering a tariff with concrete instead of price lists. This is The Planning Desk.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: Good morning, it's Wednesday the twenty-eighth of October, and I'm Anna.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: And I'm Erik.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: Quick note, this show is made with A I. A I agents gather the news, and our voices are synthetic.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Today, Audi's plant in Georgia, logistics bosses who say A I is moving too slowly, Kroger's shelf data, a new warehouse in Enköping and German insolvencies that won't come down.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: Audi will build its first plant in the United States, on the Middle Georgia Mega Site in Peach County, near Macon. The investment is four billion dollars.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Capacity is up to two hundred thousand vehicles a year, with about four thousand five hundred jobs, and construction starts in twenty twenty-seven.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: The first American-built Audis, premium S U Vs for North America, are due in the early twenty-thirties. This is a long play, not a quick fix.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Audi says the plant cuts its exposure to trade and currency risk, and that includes the fifteen percent tariff on European car imports.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: It also makes North America a third production pillar next to Europe and China, with Germany staying the industrial core, according to the company.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Germany staying the core is the line for home. The signal that matters goes to suppliers, because Audi is answering a tariff with footprint instead of pricing.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: If you supply Audi from Europe, expect part of your North American volume to move to local sourcing within the decade, and start mapping which parts that could be.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Network designers get a clean case too, one tariff, one site, and a construction start date to plan against.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Over to the A I desk. Consultancy Horváth asked transport and logistics board members and managing directors in thirty-two countries how fast A I is arriving, and eighty percent say too slowly.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: Too slow where?

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Planning, dispatching and customer service are the examples in the study. And eighty-four percent expect A I to become a central source of competitive advantage.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: A I and digital transformation climbed to the second priority this year, up from fourth in twenty twenty-five. Ninety-four percent also expect strong pressure on margins.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Here's the line I'd circle. Ninety percent say customers now care more about reliability and punctuality than about top speed.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: And every single respondent expects more cyberattacks on transport and logistics networks.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: For shippers, your carriers are about to push harder on A I in planning and dispatch. Expect their data feeds and booking interfaces to change, and ask now how those will connect to your own plans.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: From carriers to the grocery shelf. Kroger told investors on the twentieth of October that it shares computer-vision shelf data with supplier partners to improve on-shelf availability.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: It also runs an A I tool that joins twenty data pipelines into views of sales, inventory and sell-through for each item in each store, so risks show up earlier.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: Then there's radio frequency identification, R F I D, in the bakery. A pilot across about fifteen hundred stores reports ninety-eight percent read rates, counts almost seventy percent faster and half the waste.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Kroger plans R F I D in more than twenty-three hundred stores by twenty twenty-nine.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: For demand planners at those suppliers, shelf-level data sits closer to the consumer than any order does. Be ready to put it into short-term forecasting.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: To Sweden, where plumbing and heating wholesaler Dahl Sverige, part of Saint-Gobain Distribution Sweden, has leased twenty-five thousand square metres of warehouse space in Enköping.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: It comes into use step by step in the first half of twenty twenty-seven, and works alongside the central warehouse in Bålsta, which opened last year to replace Kallhäll.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Bålsta runs an automated high-bay pallet store and a shuttle for trays and cartons. Logistics director Jonathan Mankowitz says the extra space raises stock availability and adds flexibility.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: A year after automating the hub, Dahl is adding a second nearby site instead of stretching one building. Distributors in Mälardalen weighing capacity against risk should look at that two-node design.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Last, a grim forecast from credit insurer Allianz Trade, which expects twenty-five thousand nine hundred company insolvencies in Germany this year, and the same again in twenty twenty-seven.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: That follows about twenty-four thousand in twenty twenty-five, and the first half of this year was up almost seven percent. A first decline, of five percent, only comes in twenty twenty-eight.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Transport and logistics is among the hardest hit, next to construction, hospitality, automotive and machinery. Allianz Trade cites the Iran conflict, weak growth, skills shortages and high operating costs.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: It also flags knock-on risk from insolvencies abroad, along international supply chains.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Two more years of this puts supplier and carrier financial health in the risk review for every German sourcing and transport lane, not just the critical ones.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: That's the desk for Wednesday.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Back tomorrow morning, and the full week in review is out on Sunday.
